title: Timed Mixed Lab Set B

header.html: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Troubleshooting 5 tasks, Cluster Architecture 4, Services and Networking 3, Workloads 2, Storage 2)
review of every domain under time pressure
Kubernetes v1.37.0; every task in this set was executed and validated in Modules 1 to 13 (setup, failing check, solution, passing check, wrong answers rejected)

html:
1How to use this set

Same rules as Set A (Module 14): a 120-minute timer, only the allowed documentation, each task prepared with --setup, all-or-nothing scoring with --check, pass mark 66% of the points. This set uses different tasks from Set A, so do Set A first, then B a few days later.

Honest note: the tasks come from the module labs; they test speed and routine, not surprise. For surprise use the killer.sh simulator.

2Tasks

<!-- SET: m12-02-kubelet-config,m11-04-fix-missing-env,m13-04-wrong-targetport,m11-07-fix-init-container,m12-06-controller-manager-broken,m02-02-sa-clusterrole,m03-05-drain-node,m04-05-kustomize-overlay,m01-02-static-pod,m07-03-fix-service-selector,m09-03-egress-policy,m13-05-pod-dns-policy,m05-08-add-probes,m06-06-taint-toleration,m10-06-fix-pending-pvc,m10-02-static-pv-pvc -->

Set size: 16 tasks, 106 points in total. Pass mark: 66%, which is 70 points. Suggested time: 120 minutes (the labs' own time estimates add up to 110 minutes). Do the tasks in order, flag what you skip, and check your work as you would on the exam.

Task 1 (Troubleshooting, 8 points, about 8 minutes) m12-02-kubelet-config

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The node cka-worker went NotReady after someone edited the kubelet configuration. Find the problem in the kubelet logs, fix the configuration file /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on that node, and bring the node back to Ready.

Task 2 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m11-04-fix-missing-env

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app4, the Pods of the Deployment worker crash with a clear message in their logs. Read the log, then fix the Deployment (do not change the image or the command) so that the Pods run stably with the required setting DB_HOST=db.internal.

Task 3 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m13-04-wrong-targetport

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net4, the Service web has endpoints, but requests to http://web.net4 end with "connection refused". The Pods are Ready and the nginx containers listen on port 80. Fix the Service (do not touch the Deployment) so that http://web.net4 works.

Task 4 (Troubleshooting, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m11-07-fix-init-container

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app7, the Pod api is stuck in Init:0/1: its init container waits until the DNS name db resolves inside the namespace. Without changing the Pod, make the Pod start. The name db must be the name of a Service in app7 that selects the existing Pod database (label app=database, nginx on port 80).

Task 5 (Troubleshooting, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m12-06-controller-manager-broken

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace cm1, the Deployment counter (2 replicas) was created but no Pods appear and kubectl get rs shows nothing. Find the faulty control plane component on cka-control-plane and repair it so that both Pods run.

Task 6 (Architecture, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m02-02-sa-clusterrole

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create the namespace ci and a ServiceAccount deployer in it. Create a ClusterRole deploy-manager that allows get, list, create and update on deployments in the apps API group. Grant it to the ServiceAccount only inside the namespace ci (not cluster-wide).

Task 7 (Architecture, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m03-05-drain-node

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Node cka-worker2 needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict the workloads from it, leaving the DaemonSet Pods alone (Pods that use emptyDir volumes may be deleted). A Deployment web in the namespace maint (4 replicas) must still have all 4 replicas Ready afterwards, on the other nodes.

Task 8 (Architecture, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m04-05-kustomize-overlay

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web with 1 replica and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, 3 replicas, and the container image to nginx:stable-alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster.

Task 9 (Architecture, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m01-02-static-pod

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a static Pod named static-web with image nginx:alpine on the node cka-worker. Find the directory the kubelet watches for static Pod manifests from the kubelet configuration file. The Pod must run in the default namespace.

Task 10 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m07-03-fix-service-selector

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc3, the Service api does not work: requests to http://api.svc3 hang. The Deployment api (2 replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that http://api.svc3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Task 11 (Networking, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m09-03-egress-policy

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace np3, the Pod app (busybox) must only be allowed to send traffic to (a) Pods labelled app=db on TCP port 80 and (b) the cluster DNS on port 53 (UDP and TCP). All other outgoing traffic from app must be blocked. Create one NetworkPolicy named app-egress for the Pod app.

Task 12 (Troubleshooting, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m13-05-pod-dns-policy

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net5, the Pod lookup cannot resolve any cluster names (for example kubernetes.default). Find the cause in the Pod spec and recreate the Pod lookup (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) so that it uses the cluster DNS and can resolve kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local.

Task 13 (Workloads, 6 points, about 7 minutes) m05-08-add-probes

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace probes, the Deployment site (2 replicas, nginx:alpine) has no health checks. Add to its container:

  • a readiness probe: HTTP GET / on port 80, initialDelaySeconds 3, periodSeconds 5;
  • a liveness probe: HTTP GET / on port 80, initialDelaySeconds 10, periodSeconds 10. All replicas must be Ready afterwards.

Task 14 (Workloads, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m06-06-taint-toleration

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Taint the node cka-worker2 with dedicated=db:NoSchedule. In the namespace taint, create a Pod db (image nginx:alpine) that tolerates this taint and is placed on cka-worker2 using nodeSelector on the label kubernetes.io/hostname.

Task 15 (Troubleshooting, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m10-06-fix-pending-pvc

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace st6, the Pod app is stuck Pending because its PersistentVolumeClaim app-data does not bind. Find the cause and fix it so the Pod runs with the claim bound. Keep the names app and app-data, the size 1Gi and ReadWriteOnce. (A claim's StorageClass cannot be edited in place; recreate what is needed.)

Task 16 (Storage, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m10-02-static-pv-pvc

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a PersistentVolume pv-manual with capacity 2Gi, access mode ReadWriteOnce, reclaim policy Retain, StorageClass name manual and the host path /mnt/data. In the namespace st2, create a PersistentVolumeClaim claim requesting 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, StorageClass manual. The claim must be bound to pv-manual.

<!-- /SET -->

3Reference solutions

Open these only after the timer ends.

<!-- SETSOL: m12-02-kubelet-config,m11-04-fix-missing-env,m13-04-wrong-targetport,m11-07-fix-init-container,m12-06-controller-manager-broken,m02-02-sa-clusterrole,m03-05-drain-node,m04-05-kustomize-overlay,m01-02-static-pod,m07-03-fix-service-selector,m09-03-egress-policy,m13-05-pod-dns-policy,m05-08-add-probes,m06-06-taint-toleration,m10-06-fix-pending-pvc,m10-02-static-pv-pvc -->

Solution 1: m12-02-kubelet-config

ssh cka-worker 'systemctl status kubelet --no-pager | head -8'
ssh cka-worker 'journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | grep -i -E "yaml|failed|error" | tail -3'
ssh cka-worker 'sed -i "/^broken:/d" /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml && systemctl restart kubelet'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/cka-worker --timeout=180s

Solution 2: m11-04-fix-missing-env

kubectl -n app4 logs deploy/worker --tail=3
kubectl -n app4 set env deployment worker DB_HOST=db.internal
kubectl -n app4 rollout status deployment worker --timeout=120s

Solution 3: m13-04-wrong-targetport

kubectl -n net4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web -o wide
kubectl -n net4 describe svc web | grep -i -E "Port|Endpoints"
kubectl -n net4 patch svc web --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":80}]'

Solution 4: m11-07-fix-init-container

kubectl -n app7 get pod api
kubectl -n app7 logs api -c wait-db --tail=3
kubectl -n app7 expose pod database --name=db --port=80
kubectl -n app7 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/api --timeout=180s

Solution 5: m12-06-controller-manager-broken

ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl ps -a --name kube-controller-manager'
ssh cka-control-plane 'crictl logs $(crictl ps -a --name kube-controller-manager -q | head -1) 2>&1 | tail -3'
ssh cka-control-plane 'sed -i "s#ca.crtx#ca.crt#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane 'systemctl restart kubelet'   # resets the crash-loop back-off of the static Pod
kubectl -n cm1 rollout status deployment counter --timeout=180s

Solution 6: m02-02-sa-clusterrole

kubectl create ns ci
kubectl -n ci create serviceaccount deployer
kubectl create clusterrole deploy-manager --verb=get,list,create,update --resource=deployments.apps
kubectl -n ci create rolebinding deploy-manager --clusterrole=deploy-manager --serviceaccount=ci:deployer

Solution 7: m03-05-drain-node

kubectl drain cka-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl -n maint rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Solution 8: m04-05-kustomize-overlay

cat > ~/kust/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml <<Y
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod
namePrefix: prod-
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod | head -30
kubectl create ns prod
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/prod
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment prod-web --timeout=120s

Solution 9: m01-02-static-pod

ssh cka-worker 'grep staticPodPath /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml'
ssh cka-worker 'mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests && cat > /etc/kubernetes/manifests/static-web.yaml <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: static-web
spec:
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
Y'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/static-web-cka-worker --timeout=120s

Solution 10: m07-03-fix-service-selector

kubectl -n svc3 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=api
kubectl -n svc3 get svc api -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n svc3 get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n svc3 patch svc api -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'

Solution 11: m09-03-egress-policy

kubectl -n np3 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: app-egress}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
  - ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
Y
sleep 5

Solution 12: m13-05-pod-dns-policy

kubectl -n net5 get pod lookup -o jsonpath='{.spec.dnsPolicy}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n net5 exec lookup -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
kubectl -n net5 delete pod lookup --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n net5 run lookup --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl -n net5 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/lookup --timeout=120s
kubectl -n net5 exec lookup -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local

Solution 13: m05-08-add-probes

kubectl -n probes patch deployment site -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"nginx","readinessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":3,"periodSeconds":5},"livenessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":10,"periodSeconds":10}}]}}}}'
kubectl -n probes rollout status deployment site --timeout=120s

Solution 14: m06-06-taint-toleration

kubectl taint node cka-worker2 dedicated=db:NoSchedule
kubectl -n taint apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: db}
spec:
  nodeSelector: {kubernetes.io/hostname: cka-worker2}
  tolerations:
  - {key: dedicated, operator: Equal, value: db, effect: NoSchedule}
  containers:
  - {name: web, image: "nginx:alpine"}
Y
kubectl -n taint wait --for=condition=Ready pod/db --timeout=120s

Solution 15: m10-06-fix-pending-pvc

kubectl -n st6 describe pod app | grep -i -A2 "FailedScheduling"
kubectl -n st6 describe pvc app-data | grep -i -A2 events
kubectl get sc
kubectl -n st6 delete pod app --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n st6 delete pvc app-data
kubectl -n st6 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: app-data}
spec:
  storageClassName: standard
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: app}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{name: vol, mountPath: /data}]
  volumes:
  - name: vol
    persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: app-data}
Y
kubectl -n st6 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/app --timeout=120s

Solution 16: m10-02-static-pv-pvc

kubectl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pv-manual}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 2Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data}
Y
kubectl -n st2 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: claim}
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
Y
sleep 3
kubectl -n st2 get pvc claim

<!-- /SETSOL -->

4Review after the set

  1. Compare your score with Set A. Which domain improved, which did not?
  2. List every command you had to look up. Learn the five most frequent ones by heart.
  3. Redo the three slowest tasks cold.

5Recall questions

R1Why do Sets A and B use different tasks?

Show the answer

So the second set tests the routine again without repeating the same answers.

R2What does a score of 60% mean for your readiness?

Show the answer

Below the 66% pass mark: repeat the weakest domain's labs and redo the set.

R3What should you do first when the cluster context may be wrong?

Show the answer

Run the context line and check kubectl config current-context.

R4Which flag generates a manifest without creating the object?

Show the answer

--dry-run=client -o yaml.

R5What do you check after fixing a broken node or component?

Show the answer

The original symptom: kubectl get nodes or a test Pod.

R6How many minutes should you keep for review at the end?

Show the answer

About 10.
